reviews.body: **Devin Review** found 1 potential issue.

review_comments.body:
🟡 **Interleaved tool calls mix arguments** When parallel calls share an index, an id-less continuation for an earlier call attaches to the latest call. Both calls then emit incorrect arguments.
Learn more The pending map stores separate calls when distinct IDs arrive with the same provider index. An id-less continuation has no ID to distinguish those calls, so reverse insertion order cannot identify its owner. [test_tool_call_accumulation](https://github.com/livekit/agents/blob/c44e660c5a233cd60d19d788b0e019f52030e625/tests/test_plugin_mistralai_llm.py#L221-L257 "tests/test_plugin_mistralai_llm.py:221-257") establishes that such continuations are supported, while the new parallel-call test covers only complete calls. Once a continuation is attached to the wrong call, the flush emits corrupted arguments for both calls. **Example:** The stream sends `call_1` at index 0 with arguments `{"loc`, then `call_2` at index 0 with arguments `{}`. A subsequent index-0 delta with no ID and arguments `ation":"Paris"}` intended for `call_1` is appended to `call_2`, which emits `{}ation":"Paris"}`. **Recommended fix:** Disambiguate ID-less fragments before appending them when several pending calls share an index. If the provider supplies no reliable discriminator, avoid guessing the latest call and define an explicit handling strategy for ambiguous fragments; add a regression test covering interleaved continuation.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*
